newsitem.title: USA: U.S. rig count down 15 to 841 in latest week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. rig count down 15 to 841 in latest week.

text.p: The number of rigs exploring for oil and natural gas in the United States stood at 841 as of Dec. 13, down 15 from the prior week and 76 above the year-ago total of 765, Baker Hughes Inc. reported Friday.
The number of rigs drilling on land fell by 17 to 705, while rigs working offshore rose three to 114. The number of rigs active in inland waters fell by one to 22.
The biggest change in individual states occurred in Oklahoma, which showed a decrease of 11 and Texas, which showed a decrease of three. Louisiana rose by three.
A total of 364 rigs were exploring for crude oil, down two from last week. The number of rigs searching for gas fell by 13 to 475, while the number of miscellaneous drilling projects remained at two.
In Canada, the number of working rigs rose by 18 to 391 vs. 288 a year ago.
The weekly rig count reflects the number of rigs exploring for oil and gas, not those producing oil and gas.
Separately, Offshore Data Services said there were 163 rigs under contract in the U.S. Gulf as of Dec. 13, up one from the prior week.
The utilization rate for rigs working in the Gulf, based on a total fleet of 178, was 91.1 percent.
The number of working rigs in European/Mediterranean remained the same this week at 105 rigs under contract out of a total fleet of 105, a utilization rate of 100 percent.
The worldwide rig count rose one to 561 out of a total fleet of 604, making the utilization rate 92.9 percent.
